goldenPoints: MgSO4 is the drug of choice for eclampsia; calcium gluconate is its antidote
Atony is the commonest cause of PPH; oxytocin is the first drug
Never do a digital PV examination in placenta previa
Cu-T 380A works for 10 years; Pearl index counts failures per 100 woman-years
OCPs protect against ovarian and endometrial cancer — not cervical cancer
CRL in the first trimester is the most accurate measure of gestational age
Complete mole is 46XX with no fetus; partial mole is 69XXY and may have one
Letrozole is first-line for ovulation induction in PCOS
AMH is the best single test of ovarian reserve; semen analysis is the first infertility test
After vasectomy, contraception is still needed for about 3 months
intro: OBG is one of the two heaviest clinical subjects in FMGE (30 of 300 questions). The stems are short clinical vignettes: a stage of labour to name, a contraceptive fact, a FIGO stage, a drug to avoid. Revise these 14 topics and you cover the great majority of what the last five years actually asked.

branches.label: Pregnancy & Antenatal Care
leaves: CRL is the most accurate dating parameter in the first trimester
Quadruple test at 15–20 weeks screens for Down syndrome

branches.label: Labour & Delivery
leaves: Active phase from 4 cm, ≥1 cm/hour progress
AMTSL: oxytocin 10 IU IM prevents PPH

branches.label: Obstetric Emergencies
leaves: PPH: atony commonest of the 4 Ts
Previa: painless, never do a PV exam

branches.label: Medical Disorders in Pregnancy
leaves: Iron 100 mg + folic acid 500 µg daily

branches.label: Contraception
leaves: Copper IUD is the best emergency method

branches.label: Benign Gynae & Infertility
leaves: Semen analysis is the first infertility test

subject: Obstetrics & Gynaecology
tagline: Labour, contraception, gynae oncology and medical disorders in pregnancy carry the paper — 30 questions every session.

topics.oneLiner: Dilatation tells the stage: 7 cm and fully effaced is still the first stage, however strong the pains.
points: First stage: onset of true labour pains to full cervical dilatation (10 cm)
Latent phase ends and active phase begins at 4 cm dilatation (WHO labour care guide)
Satisfactory active-phase progress: cervix dilates at least 1 cm/hour in a primigravida
Second stage: full dilatation to delivery of the baby; up to 2 hours in a primigravida
Third stage: delivery of baby to expulsion of placenta and membranes, about 15–30 minutes
Fourth stage: first hour after delivery — the hour of close observation
Signs of placental separation: cord lengthening, fresh gush of blood, uterus rises and becomes globular
Ritgen manoeuvre controls delivery of the head and protects the perineum
Immediately after delivery the fundus lies at about the level of 20–22 weeks size
topics.title: Normal Labour & Its Stages
topics.trap: Full effacement is not full dilatation — a 7 cm cervix is first stage, not second.

topics.askedAs: presentation diagnosis and safest delivery route
topics.oneLiner: A brow that stays a brow and a transverse lie that stays transverse both belong to the operating theatre.
points: Face presentation: head fully extended, denominator is the mentum; mento-anterior can deliver vaginally
Brow presentation usually converts to face or vertex; persistent brow needs caesarean section
Transverse lie with a live term fetus: caesarean section is the delivery of choice
Most common cause of occipito-posterior position problems is a deflexed head
Breech: frank breech is the commonest type; footling breech has the highest cord prolapse risk
Obstructed labour signs: Bandl's ring, oedematous cervix, maternal exhaustion, fetal distress
Neglected obstructed labour ends in uterine rupture, fistula and sepsis
Trial of labour is done only with adequate pelvis, vertex presentation and full monitoring backup
topics.title: Malpresentations & Obstructed Labour
topics.trap: Vacuum (ventouse) is contraindicated in preterm babies and in face or brow presentation.

topics.oneLiner: McRoberts first, suprapubic pressure with it, fundal pressure never.
points: Shoulder dystocia: head-to-shoulder delivery interval prolonged; turtle sign is classic
First manoeuvre: McRoberts (hyperflex the mother's thighs) with suprapubic pressure
If McRoberts fails: internal manoeuvres — Rubin, Woods corkscrew, delivery of posterior arm
Fundal pressure is never applied — it worsens impaction and risks rupture
Wrigley's forceps are the outlet forceps; Kielland forceps are rotational
Vacuum is contraindicated below 34 weeks and in face, brow or breech presentation
Commonest indication for caesarean section in India: previous caesarean section
Least risk for successful TOLAC: previous lower-segment transverse scar with a prior vaginal birth
topics.title: Shoulder Dystocia & Operative Delivery
topics.trap: Students pick fundal pressure — it is the one manoeuvre that is always wrong here.

topics.askedAs: drug sequence when the uterus stays atonic
topics.oneLiner: Tone is the commonest T; oxytocin first, ergometrine never in hypertension, carboprost never in asthma.
points: PPH: blood loss ≥500 mL after vaginal birth, ≥1000 mL after caesarean section
Four causes — the 4 Ts: Tone (atony, commonest), Trauma, Tissue (retained placenta), Thrombin
First-line drug for atony: oxytocin; AMTSL uses oxytocin 10 IU IM within a minute of birth
If oxytocin fails: methylergometrine — contraindicated in hypertension and heart disease
Carboprost (15-methyl PGF2α) is the next drug — contraindicated in bronchial asthma
Misoprostol is the heat-stable backup where refrigeration is unavailable
Retained placenta beyond 30 minutes needs manual removal under anaesthesia
Acute uterine inversion presents with shock out of proportion and no palpable fundus
Bluish perineal swelling with hypotension after forceps delivery: vulvovaginal haematoma
topics.title: Postpartum Haemorrhage
topics.trap: Ergometrine in a pre-eclamptic woman — the classic wrong pairing the paper loves.

topics.askedAs: drug of choice and drugs to avoid
topics.oneLiner: MgSO4 for fits, calcium gluconate for MgSO4, delivery for cure.
points: Pre-eclampsia: BP ≥140/90 after 20 weeks with proteinuria ≥300 mg/24 hours
Severe features: BP ≥160/110, platelets <1 lakh, raised transaminases, creatinine >1.1, visual symptoms
Eclampsia is pre-eclampsia plus generalised tonic-clonic convulsions
Drug of choice to prevent and treat eclamptic fits: magnesium sulphate
MgSO4 toxicity is monitored by knee jerks, respiratory rate and urine output; antidote is calcium gluconate
Safe antihypertensives in pregnancy: labetalol, methyldopa, nifedipine, hydralazine
ACE inhibitors, ARBs and atenolol are avoided in pregnancy
HELLP syndrome: haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
Definitive treatment of severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia is delivery, whatever the gestation
topics.title: Hypertensive Disorders in Pregnancy
topics.trap: Phenytoin and diazepam are not the answer for eclampsia — magnesium sulphate is.

topics.oneLiner: Painless and soft is previa; painful and woody is abruption.
points: Placenta previa: painless, bright red bleeding; uterus soft and relaxed; fetal parts easily felt
Digital vaginal examination is contraindicated in placenta previa
A marginal placenta on mid-pregnancy scan is re-scanned around 32–36 weeks before deciding the route
Placenta accreta risk is highest with placenta previa over a previous caesarean scar
Abruptio placentae: painful bleeding, tense tender woody uterus, fetal parts difficult to feel
Abruption is the APH most associated with DIC and Couvelaire uterus
Concealed abruption can present with shock and a tense abdomen with little visible bleeding
APH is bleeding from the genital tract after 28 weeks (viability) and before birth
topics.title: Antepartum Haemorrhage: Previa vs Abruption
topics.trap: Doing a PV examination in suspected previa can trigger catastrophic bleeding — never.

topics.askedAs: GDM values, anaemia doses, safe drugs
topics.oneLiner: DIPSI 140 at 2 hours, iron 100 mg with folic acid 500 µg — two numbers FMGE repeats.
points: DIPSI criteria: single-step 75 g OGTT; 2-hour value ≥140 mg/dL diagnoses GDM in India
GDM risks: macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, neonatal hypoglycaemia after birth
Pregnancy iron prophylaxis under the national programme: 100 mg elemental iron with 500 µg folic acid
Women on antiepileptic drugs need high-dose folic acid (5 mg/day) from before conception
Anaemia in pregnancy (WHO): haemoglobin below 11 g/dL
Heart disease with the worst maternal prognosis: Eisenmenger syndrome
Supine hypotension syndrome: aortocaval compression by the gravid uterus; turn the woman left lateral
Live vaccines are contraindicated in pregnancy; toxoids and killed vaccines are allowed
Physiological changes: plasma volume and GFR rise, haemoglobin concentration falls by dilution
topics.title: Medical Disorders in Pregnancy
topics.trap: Rubella and other live vaccines in pregnancy — contraindicated; only killed/toxoid vaccines are safe.

topics.askedAs: abortion type from findings, MTP limits
topics.oneLiner: Os open or closed, fetus alive or dead — two questions classify almost every abortion stem.
points: Threatened abortion: bleeding with a closed os and a live fetus — pregnancy can continue
Inevitable abortion: os open, membranes ruptured or products not yet expelled
Missed abortion: fetus dead, os closed, uterus smaller than dates
Septic abortion follows instrumentation with unsterile technique; can progress to septic shock
Suction evacuation is the surgical method of choice in the first trimester (up to 12 weeks)
MTP Amendment 2021: up to 20 weeks on one doctor's opinion; 20–24 weeks needs two, for notified categories
Medical abortion: mifepristone followed 24–48 hours later by misoprostol
Recurrent pregnancy loss workup includes antiphospholipid antibody syndrome and parental karyotyping
Cervical incompetence: painless mid-trimester loss; treated with cervical cerclage (McDonald stitch)
topics.title: Early Pregnancy: Abortion & MTP
topics.trap: Missed abortion has a closed os; inevitable has an open os — the stems swap them deliberately.

topics.oneLiner: Ampulla for ectopic; 46XX and no fetus for complete mole, 69XXY with fetus for partial.
points: Commonest site of ectopic pregnancy: ampulla of the fallopian tube
Risk factors: PID, previous ectopic, tubal surgery, IUCD failure, assisted reproduction
Pregnancy of unknown location: serial β-hCG — a subnormal rise suggests ectopic or failing pregnancy
Methotrexate is used only in a haemodynamically stable, unruptured ectopic meeting size and hCG criteria
Ruptured ectopic with shock: resuscitate and operate — salpingectomy if the tube is destroyed
Complete mole: 46XX, entirely paternal (androgenetic), no fetal parts, p57 negative
Partial mole: triploid 69XXY, fetal parts may be present, p57 positive
Mole on ultrasound: snowstorm / bunch-of-grapes appearance; follow-up is serial β-hCG
Choriocarcinoma can follow a mole, abortion or even a normal pregnancy and spreads by blood
topics.title: Ectopic Pregnancy & Molar Pregnancy
topics.trap: An XY complete mole is a distractor — complete moles are 46XX (or 46XY rarely); XY edematous villi point elsewhere.

topics.oneLiner: Pearl index measures failure; copper IUD is the best emergency method; vasectomy works only after 3 months.
points: Pearl index: pregnancies per 100 woman-years of exposure — lower means more effective
Cu-T 380A is effective for 10 years; LNG-IUS (52 mg) for up to 5–8 years by type
Commonest side effect after Cu-IUD insertion: increased menstrual bleeding and pain
Emergency contraception: levonorgestrel 1.5 mg single dose, best within 72 hours
Most effective emergency contraception: copper IUD, usable up to 5 days after intercourse
Ulipristal acetate is effective up to 120 hours (5 days)
Combined pills protect against ovarian and endometrial cancer and PID — not against cervical cancer or STIs
After vasectomy, another method is needed until azoospermia is confirmed, about 3 months
Absolute contraindications to combined pills include migraine with aura and past thromboembolism
topics.title: Contraception
topics.trap: OCPs do NOT protect against cervical cancer — that is the recurring 'except' answer.

topics.oneLiner: Oestrogen ferns and triggers the LH surge; progesterone runs the secretory phase.
points: First sign of puberty in girls: thelarche (breast budding); menarche comes later
LH surge is triggered by sustained high oestrogen exerting positive feedback
Ferning of dried cervical mucus is an oestrogen effect; progesterone makes mucus thick and scanty
Progesterone acts on the post-ovulatory endometrium to make it secretory
Primary amenorrhoea with cyclical pain and a bulging bluish membrane: imperforate hymen with haematocolpos
Asherman syndrome: intrauterine adhesions after curettage — amenorrhoea with normal hormone levels
Asherman on HSG gives a honeycomb / filling-defect picture
Turner syndrome (45,XO): short stature, webbed neck, widely spaced nipples, streak ovaries
Prolactinoma: amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea, bitemporal hemianopia; first test is serum prolactin
topics.title: Menstrual Physiology, Puberty & Amenorrhoea
topics.trap: Amenorrhoea after D&C with normal hormones is Asherman — an uterine cause, not ovarian failure.

topics.oneLiner: Rotterdam 2-of-3 for PCOS; laparoscopy is gold standard for endometriosis; hyaline is the fibroid's commonest degeneration.
points: PCOS: Rotterdam criteria — any 2 of oligo-anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries on USG
First-line management of PCOS: weight loss and lifestyle change
Letrozole is the first-line drug for ovulation induction in PCOS
Ovarian drilling is a surgical option for clomiphene/letrozole-resistant PCOS
Endometriosis: dysmenorrhoea, dyspareunia, infertility, fixed retroverted uterus, uterosacral nodules
Gold standard for diagnosing endometriosis: laparoscopy with biopsy
Endometrioma on USG: ground-glass 'chocolate cyst' appearance
Fibroid: commonest benign tumour of the uterus; commonest degeneration is hyaline
Red degeneration of fibroid occurs in pregnancy and presents with acute pain
topics.title: PCOS, Endometriosis, Fibroids & AUB
topics.trap: A simple 6 cm unilocular ovarian cyst with normal markers in an asymptomatic woman needs observation, not surgery.

topics.oneLiner: HPV 16/18 for the cervix, CA-125 for serous ovarian, radical hysterectomy for stage IB cervix.
points: Cervical cancer: HPV 16 is the commonest oncogenic type; 16 and 18 cause most cases
Postcoital bleeding with a friable cervical growth: carcinoma cervix until proved otherwise
Stage IB cervical cancer is commonly treated with radical (Wertheim) hysterectomy
Point A in cervical brachytherapy lies 2 cm above and 2 cm lateral to the external os
Cervarix covers HPV 16 and 18; Gardasil also covers 6 and 11 (wart types)
Endometrial cancer risk rises with unopposed oestrogen, obesity, diabetes and nulliparity
Endometrial carcinoma reaching the vagina or parametrium is FIGO stage III disease
Hyperplasia without atypia is managed with progestins; with atypia, hysterectomy is preferred
Commonest ovarian malignancy: serous cystadenocarcinoma (epithelial); marker CA-125
topics.title: Gynaecological Oncology & Screening
topics.trap: Postmenopausal bleeding is least likely from fibroids — always exclude endometrial cancer first.

topics.askedAs: first test, best test, cause of fistula
topics.oneLiner: Semen first, AMH for reserve, tube for genital TB, obstructed labour for fistula.
points: First investigation in infertility: semen analysis — simplest and rules out the male factor
Best test of ovarian reserve: anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH)
HSG showing bilateral fluid-filled S-shaped tubes: hydrosalpinx
Commonest site of genital tuberculosis: the fallopian tube
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY): tall stature, gynaecomastia, small testes, azoospermia
Low count + poor motility + abnormal forms together is called oligoasthenoteratozoospermia
Grade 3 uterovaginal prolapse with a pressure (decubitus) ulcer: heal the ulcer before surgery
Continuous dribbling of urine days after obstructed labour or caesarean: vesicovaginal fistula
Bartholin cyst sits at the posterolateral vaginal opening; marsupialisation is the treatment of choice
topics.title: Infertility, Prolapse, Fistula & Common Gynae Problems
topics.trap: Bacterial vaginosis is not an STI and shows clue cells — do not confuse it with trichomonas (frothy green discharge, strawberry cervix).
